NVDA.rationale: NVDA delivers exceptional fundamental health and trajectory: Q1 FY2026 revenue of $81.61B (+85.2% YoY), EPS of $2.39 (+214.5% YoY), gross margin of 74.9%, operating margin of 65.6%, and operating cash flow of $50.34B in a single quarter. The balance sheet is fortress-grade with 4.3% debt-to-equity. Valuation is at the floor of its own history: PE of 33.4x vs. 32.3-66.8x range, PB of 27.3x vs. 26.3-57.8x range, despite delivering the strongest quarterly earnings ever. The implied PEG of ~0.15x is extremely low if growth persists even at a fraction of current pace. The franchise is dominant (~86% AI GPU market share, CUDA ecosystem with 5M+ developers, 75% gross margins) with structural growth vectors extending beyond GPUs: Vera CPU targeting $200B TAM, physical AI at $9B+ TTM revenue, networking revenue surging 199% YoY. Capital allocation has pivoted decisively toward shareholder returns ($80B buyback authorization, 25x dividend increase, 50%+ FCF return commitment). Near-term catalyst: Computex 2026 (June 1-4) unveiled Vera CPU, Vera Rubin platform, and RTX Spark, with fall 2026 shipments creating a re-rating window. However, the score is capped below +0.5 by: (1) negative equity risk premium (3.0% earnings yield vs. 4.47% 10Y Treasury), (2) customer concentration risk (~50% from five hyperscalers), (3) China export controls now zeroing out that market, (4) rising long rates mechanically compressing duration-sensitive valuations, and (5) growth durability uncertainty — a single quarter of +85% revenue growth is inherently difficult to sustain. The PE compression from 56.2x to 33.4x in one month reflects the market pricing some normalization, but the stock has not fully caught up to the earnings inflection (still ~7.5% below ATH).
